E1.thought: A sixteen-feature prior-season role profile (the fifteen listed plus routes per game: routes, TPRR, first-read share, alignment, XFP) would improve next-season targets, receptions and yards per game over the player's own prior production.
E1.result: REJECTED by the registered rule. The challenger was 3% WORSE than the baseline model on all three outcomes (better in only 1 of 3 test seasons). It lost in the first two test seasons, when it was trained on about 100 rows, and won in 2025 after more training data, the signature of an over-parameterised model rather than evidence that role carries no information. Sensitivity (QA): the challenger loses at ridge penalties 1e-6, 1 and 10 and 'wins' at 100 only because the baseline itself gets worse; against the best baseline across penalties the best challenger is 0.5-0.9% worse. The registered label REJECTED means no evidence of a gain; with about 250 test rows the interval is wide, so it does not prove the role profile carries no information.
E1.action: Do not use the fifteen-feature profile. The compact version E6 is exploratory and cannot support promotion; confirm it on 2026 weekly data.

E2.thought: Opportunity (XFP/G) of the prior season predicts next-season fantasy production better than results (FP/G) alone, because touchdown and efficiency variance does not persist.
E2.result: FP/G: PROMISING by the registered rule (1.24% lower MAE at the registered ridge penalty, CI excludes 0 at 97.5%, better in 3 of 3 seasons) but FRAGILE: the gain is 0.48% with unpenalised OLS, 0.62% at penalty 1, 0.99% if players with 4+ next-season games are kept (0.9% at 1+), 2024 is a tie (0.02%), and adding raw prior targets and carries per game to the baseline leaves XFP only a 0.19% gain whose interval includes 0 (FP/G and XFP/G correlate 0.97). TD/G: INCONCLUSIVE (0.47%). Registered overall status: INCONCLUSIVE. Not a proven signal.
E2.action: Do not treat XFP as a demonstrated improvement over volume. Possible next step is a pre-registered test of Fantasy Points XFP against GOING's own nflverse ff_opportunity expected usage and against raw volume, with the E2 population and the 99.78% multiplicity-adjusted interval in mind (it barely excludes zero).

E3.thought: Prior-season role features add to what GOING already knows in-season (rolling usage), most in weeks 1-4.
E3.result: Not supported. In weeks 1-4 the challenger was 1.0% worse (yards) and 0.4% worse (receptions) and 0.3% better (targets, inconclusive) than the baseline that already contains prior averages and rolling in-season usage. Later buckets were consistently worse. Separately, in-season rolling usage clearly matters: it lowers MAE by 3.3-5.0% in weeks 1-4 and 5-12% later versus prior-season averages alone. Caveats from QA: nflverse weekly rows are missing for some games a player appeared in (about 2 per player-season), so zero-stat weeks are under-represented in training and test; the in-season baseline B2 is a linear blend without a games-played interaction (a stronger blend B2x improves it by 0.5-0.9% and the challenger is still worse); B2 does not include GOING's own ff_opportunity, so E3 compares against a proxy for the Champion.
E3.action: Do not add Fantasy Points role features to weekly volume projections on this evidence. Make sure GOING's early-season props blend prior-season averages with in-season usage (large measured gain).

E4.thought: A receiver's man-vs-zone advantage interacts with how much man coverage the opponent played, improving weekly yardage prediction.
E4.result: REJECTED. The interaction term did not improve prediction (receiving yards 0.2% worse, targets unchanged; CIs include 0; 0 of 2 test seasons better). Test seasons are few (2024, 2025) and the opponent signal is a prior-season average, so power is limited.
E4.action: No matchup badge built on this signal. Revisit with 2026 same-season coverage frequencies when enough weekly snapshots exist.

E5.thought: Script-split pass rates predict next season's overall pass rate better than the overall rate alone.
E5.result: Point estimate 2.4% worse (REJECTED by the registered v1 rule). The interval [-0.105, +0.263] on a 3.01 baseline is compatible with up to a 3.5% gain, so with about 96 team-seasons this is effectively INCONCLUSIVE.
E5.action: No evidence of an edge; no action. A rejecting rule that requires the interval to exclude a worthwhile gain (v2) now applies to all newly registered experiments.

E6.thought: (Exploratory, post-hoc after E1) three compact role features add to the production baseline without E1's overfit.
E6.result: INCONCLUSIVE: 0.6-1.4% lower MAE, better in 2 of 3 seasons, but the confidence intervals include 0 (about 250 test players). Directionally positive, not demonstrated.
E6.action: Needs prospective data. Cannot support promotion because it was designed after seeing E1 on the same seasons.

E7.thought: The production 80% current-season / 20% earlier-season weighting is too aggressive in the first weeks; a blend whose prior counts as c pseudo-games predicts the weekly mean better.
E7.result: PROMISING (historical, mean accuracy by MAE) in 4 of 8 markets, weeks 1-6 vs the reconstructed Champion: QB passing yards -6.7% MAE and QB passing TDs -6.2% (3/3 seasons; equal-weight windows do as well, c about 3-4), receptions -1.2% and receiving yards -1.3% (3/3 seasons, c about 1-2; the gain comes almost entirely from players with exactly one current-season game, where the Champion puts 80% of the weight on a single game). All-weeks gains are smaller (QB 2.3-2.5%; receiving 0.4-0.5%, REJECTED under the registered v2 rule). Touchdown markets and rushing yards showed no MAE difference, but MAE is the wrong loss for 0/1-like outcomes (QA): see E7b, which uses the Poisson log score. The repo's 2026 season review reports a similar direction for equal vs 80/20 weights; that is a separate, unaudited analysis and is not independent confirmation.
E7.action: Strongest evidence so far that the Champion can be improved, and it is about WEIGHTING, not Fantasy Points. Candidate Challenger: replace 0.8/0.2 with k/(k+c) shrinkage. Not promoted: it improves the projected mean, not demonstrated on market prices (no historical prop lines), and the 2026 prospective check (E10) is too small to say.

E8.thought: Expected-opportunity information adds to the Champion's mean, and Fantasy Points XFP adds something beyond ffopportunity.
E8.result: Fantasy Points XFP added nothing beyond ffopportunity on any market (MEOFP vs MEOP: rec_tds -0.1%, rec_yds +0.1%, receptions +0.1%, rush_yds 0.0%, rush_tds +1.4%; all INCONCLUSIVE or REJECTED). The first-run reading that ffopportunity helped is NOT established: that baseline had no raw volume, so most of the gain is target/carry counts (raw volume alone gave rec_yds +1.6% and rec_tds +4.3%) and in-season recency. See E8b for the corrected comparison. FP XFP vs the Champion alone (rush_yds +1.1%, rush_tds +3.1%, borderline) also lacked raw carries, so it reflects raw volume, not expected-points quality.
E8.action: Fantasy Points XFP is redundant with free ffopportunity and with raw volume. Use E8b for any opportunity claim.

E9.thought: Bell-cow role shares and role stability add to Champion plus raw volume for carries, rushing yards and rushing TDs; efficiency metrics do not.
E9.result: INCONCLUSIVE overall: none of the four blocks beat Champion plus raw volume. Advanced rushing efficiency was worse than the baseline in every outcome (as hypothesised: efficiency does not persist); bell-cow shares and ffopportunity rushing expectation added nothing; role stability was +0.5% carries and +0.25% rushing yards (inconclusive).
E9.action: Do not add bell-cow or advanced-rushing fields as predictors. Raw carry/target volume already captures the signal. Revisit role stability with 2026 weekly states.

E10.thought: The E7 blend would have improved the probabilities the production system actually froze in 2026.
E10.result: INCONCLUSIVE: after fixing the date join (Eastern game date, one record per contract) 179 settled 2026 receptions predictions in 16 games match the reconstructed Champion; the blend (c=1) changed Brier by 0.04% (0.2480 vs 0.2481; CI -0.0026 to +0.0037). Only 11 of those had at most 2 current-season games, which is where the blend is supposed to matter, so the check is uninformative rather than negative. QB markets: 23 predictions, 3 early-season; descriptive only.
E10.action: Keep E7 as a Challenger; re-run each week. No production change.

E7b.thought: (Exploratory, post-hoc after QA) For count markets the prior-strength blend, chosen and judged by Poisson log score, beats the Champion's 80/20 weighting in weeks 1-6.
E7b.result: All five count markets cleared the pre-registered bar in 3 of 3 test seasons (mean log-score gain per row: receptions +0.062, receiving TD +0.035, rushing TD +0.038, anytime TD +0.044, QB passing TD +0.092 nats; adjusted CIs exclude 0; chosen c = 2 for receptions, 3-4 for the rest). Capped at NEEDS PROSPECTIVE DATA because it was designed after E7. Caveat: the log score floors a predicted mean at 0.01, so part of the gain comes from players whose Champion mean is at or near zero (a zero Poisson mean gives a huge penalty when the event happens); how production prices a zero mean was not audited here, so some of this gain may not exist in the live probabilities. The TD gains are the most likely to be partly this artefact.
E7b.action: Challenger idea: shrink toward the prior-season mean for count markets and never let a mean reach zero. Verify how production handles zero means, then test on 2026 prices before anything is promoted.

E8b.thought: (Exploratory, post-hoc after QA) Expected-opportunity sources add information beyond raw volume, including raw in-season volume.
E8b.result: Fantasy Points XFP/XTD added nothing beyond raw volume (MFP vs MV: REJECTED in all five markets) nor beyond ffopportunity (MEOFP vs MEO: REJECTED in all five). ffopportunity prior-season expectation beyond raw volume (MEOP vs MV): INCONCLUSIVE for receiving yards (+0.6%), nothing elsewhere. ffopportunity in-season rolling expected values beyond in-season raw volume (MEO vs MVR): receptions +2.9%, receiving yards +1.2% and rushing yards +1.0%, each better in 3 of 3 seasons with an adjusted CI above the bar; no gain for either TD market. Capped at NEEDS PROSPECTIVE DATA (post-hoc). Caveat: the ffopportunity expected-value model's training period was not verified and may include 2023-2025, which would flatter this result.
E8b.action: Challenger idea: in-season ffopportunity expected receptions/yards/rushing yards as a mean adjustment. Free data. Confirm the ffopportunity fitting period and run it prospectively on 2026 before any use. Fantasy Points XFP is not needed.

P3-1.thought: A learned prior-strength blend beats the fixed 80/20 weighting in the first six weeks without hurting later weeks (develop 2021-23, validate 2024, confirm 2025).
P3-1.result: PROMISING in 6 of 8 markets: receptions, receiving yards, receiving TD, rushing TD, anytime TD, passing TD (both years, holdout intervals above zero, all-weeks not worse). Early-week gains: receptions +0.05-0.07 nats/row, receiving yards MAE -1.0%/-1.9%, TD markets +0.03-0.05 nats. Passing yards (-6.7%/-4.4% MAE but only 170 rows) and rushing yards are INCONCLUSIVE. 2025 is a confirmation holdout, not a clean one. Independent QA reproduced the receptions and receiving-yards numbers with separate code.
P3-1.action: Candidate Champion v2 for the six markets and validated positions (docs/CHAMPION_V2.md); passing and rushing yards stay shadow.

P3-2.thought: What changed in a receiver's routes, target quality, alignment, expected points or team pass environment over his last 1/3/6 games predicts next-game targets and yards beyond the Champion and raw recency.
P3-2.result: Only the ROLE block (routes, route participation, TPRR, target share) helped: targets +2.0%, receiving yards +1.3%, receptions +1.4% MAE in all 3 seasons; the last game is the best single window and level+trend beats either alone. Target quality (first read, designed, air-yards share, aDOT), deployment (slot/wide/inline), Fantasy Points XFP, free ffopportunity and team pass environment added nothing.
P3-2.action: See P3-4: the ROLE gain is reproduced by free nflverse snap share.

P3-3.thought: Rushing role, expected opportunity, goal-line usage and efficiency trends predict next-game carries and rushing yards beyond Champion + raw recency.
P3-3.result: RUROLE (snap %, carry share, target share, route %) lifted carries +1.8% (3/3 seasons) and rushing yards +0.9% (inconclusive). XFP/expected-yards, goal-line and efficiency blocks, ffopportunity and team environment: no gain; XFP beyond ffopportunity was slightly worse.
P3-3.action: No bell-cow or efficiency feature is a predictor beyond role share.

P3-4.thought: (Exploratory follow-up) The ROLE gain is carried by free nflverse snap/target/carry share; Fantasy Points routes and bell-cow shares add nothing further.
P3-4.result: Free role signals beat baseline: targets +2.4%, receiving yards +1.5%, carries +1.8%, rushing yards +1.0% (3/3 seasons, snap share the strongest component). Fantasy Points role fields added +0.2% at most (rushing worse): their intervals exclude a 1% gain. Capped at NEEDS PROSPECTIVE DATA (post-hoc).
P3-4.action: Candidate Challenger on free data only: a role layer on the Champion mean. Run it in shadow on 2026; do not buy or ship Fantasy Points role fields for prediction.

P3-5.thought: Counts are overdispersed: a negative binomial prices count thresholds better than Poisson.
P3-5.result: True for receptions only (phi 0.2: +0.02-0.03 nats/row, Brier +0.6-1.4%, both years). Touchdown markets show no gain; passing TDs are not overdispersed. Zero-inflated Poisson adds nothing reliable.
P3-5.action: Receptions NB is ready as a patch (parked: it changes hashed generator code of the today-ranking-v1 experiment).

P3-6.thought: The production per-window yardage spread is poorly estimated; a pooled spread per position prices thresholds better.
P3-6.result: Production 80% intervals cover only 69-76% of outcomes. Pooled spread improves pinball loss 2.5-5.4% (receiving and passing yards) in both years; rushing yards is inconclusive. QB spread sat at the grid edge (0.4).
P3-6.action: Receiving yards goes with the blend; passing yards stays shadow.

P3-6b.thought: (Exploratory) A finer spread grid and a player/pool shrinkage improve P3-6.
P3-6b.result: QB cv 0.3, same gains (+5.4%/+3.6% passing, +2.5%/+2.9% receiving pinball). Tail coverage still imperfect for QBs. Capped at NEEDS PROSPECTIVE DATA.
P3-6b.action: Parameters used for receiving yards only; passing yards in shadow.

P3-7.thought: Champion v2 means lower the error of next-game DraftKings projections.
P3-7.result: QB core-component DK points MAE -1.9%/-2.8% (weeks 1-6 -4%/-7%), WR +0.5%/+1.4% (inconclusive), RB and TE no change. The first run mis-scored quarterback rushing (a bug, fixed and rerun; the corrected run is the one on file).
P3-7.action: DFS inherits the betting-side mean gains for QB; elsewhere no measurable change.

P3-8.thought: A within-player copula and the v2 chain give better DraftKings floor/median/ceiling quantiles than independent components.
P3-8.result: Independent components cover only 62-72% of outcomes in the central 80% interval; the copula with measured correlations (receptions-yards .74-.75, yards-TD .19-.20, QB passing yards-TD .43) reaches 73-82% and improves pinball 3-8% against the old chain, in both years.
P3-8.action: Used by shared/dfs-sim.js; projection SD now comes from the simulation, not the independent-variance sum.

P3-9.thought: Measured role-pair correlations make stack-total forecasts better calibrated than independence.
P3-9.result: QB-WR1 .34, QB-WR2 .25, QB-TE1 .21, QB-RB1 .07, QB-opposing QB .13; QB-opposing WR1 .03 (interval spans zero) and WR1-WR2 .01: no measurable bring-back or teammate-competition effect. Stack total spread (PIT sd) improves from 1.19-1.29 to 1.04-1.14; pinball +1.0-1.7% for four of five stacks.
P3-9.action: Measured correlations replace the heuristic stack and bring-back bonuses in the new build style.
